findings.title: Unauthenticated database read/write endpoints
source_evidence: src/middleware/index.js:7-18 chain ALS, cors origin *, helmet, morgan, json, urlencoded; no auth middleware
src/index.js:11,32-34 applyMiddleware then app.use /api routes; no auth gate
src/routes/index.js:8-9,11,20,29 and src/routes/workflow.js:21,38,55,68,89,105,121,196,205,240-241,255,285 handlers reach sql with no user or token check
package.json:12-18 no auth validation or rate-limit deps; zero auth hits in src
findings.trace: Unauthenticated HTTP client to Express handler with no credential check to neon sql tagged-template query to Postgres to res.json row. Examples: GET /api/users SELECT users; POST /api/users INSERT INTO users; GET /api/workflow/identifiers SELECT star from workflow_identifiers.
findings.resource: Tables users, workflow_identifiers, workflow_events, work_identifiers, domain_datastore
findings.outcome: Unauthorized read plus create and update of records without credential
findings.impact: Exposes all workflow and user data operations to the internet; enabler for IDOR, event forgery, and context manipulation findings
findings.remediation: Enforce authentication on /api with API key or JWT verification and default deny; restrict CORS to an allowlist; add per-workflow authorization; add rate limiting.

findings.title: Workflow IDOR and missing ownership authorization
source_evidence: src/services/workflowIdentifier.js:99-127 getWorkflowIdentifier lookup by identifier only, 404 if missing, no principal
src/services/workflowIdentifier.js:132-166 listWorkflowIdentifiers SELECT star with status and workflow_id only
src/services/workflowIdentifier.js:171-207 updateWorkflowIdentifier existence check only then UPDATE and RETURNING star
src/services/workflowDecider.js:142-156 fetchWorkflowRow existence check only; 374-394 and 533-549 accept WORKFLOW_ID or workflow_identifier or workflow_id or id
src/services/workflowIdentifier.js:8-11 identifier uses Date.now plus Math.random, not CSPRNG
findings.trace: Request identifier from params query or body to get list update or fetchWorkflowRow to sql WHERE workflow_identifier or workflow_id to existence-only check to full row plus events returned or updated. GET /identifiers lists all workflows without auth so no guessing is needed.
findings.principal: Any unauthenticated caller acting against another workflow owner or data subject
findings.resource: Arbitrary workflow_identifiers record plus workflow_events history plus work_identifiers events plus domain_datastore data
findings.outcome: Cross-workflow read and mutation of any workflow by listing or knowing its identifier
findings.impact: cross-workflow read, update, advance, or fork of any loan workflow
findings.remediation: Require authenticated principal; add owner or tenant column and enforce WHERE identifier plus owner equals auth subject; use crypto.randomUUID for identifiers; remove or protect bulk GET /identifiers.

findings.title: Unauthenticated DDL-via-POST endpoints
source_evidence: src/routes/workflow.js:55-62 POST /createdb calls createWorkIdentifierTable with no auth
src/routes/workflow.js:285-292 POST /createDomainDatastoreTable calls createDomainDatastoreTable with no auth
src/config/db.js:67-78 CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS work_identifiers fixed string
src/services/domainDatastore.js:8-19 CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS domain_datastore fixed string
src/config/db.js:10-65 initDb runs same DDL at boot so runtime role already holds CREATE
findings.trace: Unauthenticated POST to /createdb or /createDomainDatastoreTable to service function to sql CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS to Postgres schema. Statements are fixed IF NOT EXISTS strings, so no arbitrary DDL demonstrated.
findings.resource: Database schema; work_identifiers and domain_datastore tables
findings.outcome: Unauthenticated triggering of schema operations plus disclosure of table names and structure in success messages
findings.impact: Schema-management surface exposed to the internet; confirms table structure; wasted DB work
findings.remediation: Delete both POST DDL routes; run DDL only via boot migration or offline migration with owner role; use a least-privilege runtime DB user without CREATE.

findings.title: Workflow event forgery and state manipulation via self-asserted actor and step
findings.correction: Phase 3 correction preserved: stamped actor is overwritten from the flow definition when the asserted step is known (getActorForState(step) fallback requestActor). The caller can still assert an attacker-chosen valid step against an arbitrary workflow with no ownership or sequence enforcement.
source_evidence: src/routes/workflow.js:121-194 recorder-decider plus 196-203 recorder events plus 205-212 decider plus 219-238 navigator plus 255-279 eventCreaterAndProcesser all pass req.body into realdecider decideNextState appendWorkflowEvent
src/services/workflowDecider.js:292-300 authorativeActor equals getActorForState(completedStep) fallback requestActor
src/services/workflowDecider.js:506-524 resolveStateKey exact then singular plural then case-insensitive
src/services/workflowDecider.js:533-580 realdecider validates presence only, fetches row by existence, publishes transition, then decisionManager without ownership or successor check
src/services/workflowDecider.js:596-629 decisionManager never calls resolveNodeForActor; actor check exists only in read-path decideNextState
src/services/workflowRecorder.js:85-123 appendWorkflowEvent appends verbatim req.body as JSON; routing heuristic is includes dash and length 36
src/services/eventPublisher.js:16-50 appends eventName to events.states and sets currentState equal eventName
findings.trace: Attacker body with WORKFLOW_ID plus WORKFLOW_ACTOR plus CURRENTCOMPLETEDSTEP to resolveStateKey to fetchWorkflowRow existence-only to publishStateTransition with definition-derived actor to eventPublisher append to states and currentState to decisionManager edge evaluation for asserted step. No check that requester owns the step or that the step follows stored currentState.
findings.principal: Any unauthenticated caller acting against another workflow borrower lender or manager
findings.resource: work_identifiers events states and currentState; workflow_events events_json
findings.outcome: Forge advance rewind or fork of any workflow history and force edge evaluation from an attacker-chosen node
findings.impact: Workflow integrity loss: fabricated state transitions and manipulated loan progression
findings.remediation: Authenticate WORKFLOW_ACTOR; enforce getActorForState(step) equals authenticated actor and step is a legal successor of stored currentState; schema-validate event bodies instead of verbatim append.

findings.title: Rule-engine context manipulation through client-controlled formData
source_evidence: src/routes/workflow.js:259-272 formData defaults to empty object then dispatchEventTypeStorage then realdecider with no null guard
src/services/domainDatastore.js:565-575 allowlist EVENTYPE_HANDLER_MAP; unknown eventType returns null but route continues

src/services/domainDatastore.js:153,168-169,264,268,301-302 salary business bank statement document consent use not-false or fallback-true defaults
src/services/domainDatastore.js:509-532 upsertAllDomains deep merge then write; 586-601 buildWorkflowContext returns stored data as rule context
src/services/ruleEngine.js:1-62 dot-path field lookup with equals not-equals greater less operators
FLOWDESINGER.json ED02 ADDRESS flags, ED03 ED04 DOCUMENTS identity flags, plus ELIGIBILITY and verification gates
findings.trace: Unauthenticated req.body formData to callDynamic eventype handler to patch to upsertAllDomains into domain_datastore data to buildWorkflowContext to evaluateRuleEngine context against edges for asserted step to nextState. Hardcoded and fallback-true flags auto-satisfy gates such as ADDRESS_INFO_SUBMITTED satisfying ED02.
findings.principal: Any unauthenticated caller; victim is lending-decision integrity and all workflow participants
findings.resource: Authoritative domain_datastore data context and ED01 through ED61 transitions
findings.outcome: Caller-controlled verification and consent flags become trusted decision inputs and drive next-node outcomes
findings.impact: Decision bypass: unverified address KYC bank consent and approval signals can be asserted as passing
findings.remediation: Fail closed by default with false FAILED or PENDING; never derive VERIFIED or consent from absent client fields; separate client form fields from verifier-attested fields written only by trusted services; schema-validate formData; abort when dispatch returns null.

findings.title: Credential-shaped DATABASE_URL exposed in tracked .env.example
findings.validity_testing: Credential validity was NOT tested. No connection to Neon was attempted. Exposure of the credential-shaped secret in the tracked repository is itself the confirmed issue.
source_evidence: .env.example:2 DATABASE_URL postgresql URI for user neondb_owner with npg_-prefixed password on Neon host ep-shiny-violet-aynt6xo8-pooler.c-5.us-east-2.aws.neon.tech database neondb
.gitignore:2 ignores .env but the example file carrying the secret is tracked
src/config/db.js:4-8 this exact DATABASE_URL authenticates the neon client as neondb_owner
findings.trace: Tracked .env.example containing credential-shaped DATABASE_URL to anyone with repository read access such as clone fork or CI logs to potential authentication as neondb_owner to Neon neondb. No live authentication step was performed.
findings.resource: Neon neondb database accessed as neondb_owner
findings.outcome: Disclosure of a privileged-looking database credential; potential full database access if the credential is live
findings.impact: Repository-wide secret exposure; treat as compromised until rotated
findings.remediation: Immediately rotate and revoke the exposed password; replace the file value with a non-secret placeholder; purge or rotate given git history retention; add secret scanning and a pre-commit hook.

rejected.reason: No SQL injection sink found. All values including status, workflow_id, identifiers, limit, offset, and JSON strings flow through neon sql tagged-template parameters. No string-concatenated SQL and no dynamic table or column names were found. LIMIT OFFSET NaN is a robustness issue, not an injection primitive.
